classification.difficultyReason: Determine missing signed ratios in quadrants II and III, then substitute into the cosine addition identity.

content.prompt:
If $\sin A=\dfrac23$, where $\dfrac\pi2<A<\pi$, and $\tan B=\dfrac23$, where $\pi<B<\dfrac{3\pi}2$, show that:
$$\cos(A+B)=\frac{3\sqrt5+4}{3\sqrt{13}}.$$

answer.worked:
By drawing a triangle in quadrant II, the adjacent side has magnitude $\sqrt{3^2-2^2}=\sqrt5$. Hence
$$\cos A=-\frac{\sqrt5}{3}.$$
By drawing a triangle in quadrant III, the hypotenuse is $\sqrt{3^2+2^2}=\sqrt{13}$. Hence
$$\sin B=-\frac2{\sqrt{13}},\qquad\cos B=-\frac3{\sqrt{13}}.$$
$$\begin{aligned}\cos(A+B)&=\cos A\cos B-\sin A\sin B\\&=\left(-\frac{\sqrt5}{3}\right)\left(-\frac3{\sqrt{13}}\right)-\left(\frac23\right)\left(-\frac2{\sqrt{13}}\right)\\&=\frac{3\sqrt5}{3\sqrt{13}}+\frac4{3\sqrt{13}}\\&=\frac{3\sqrt5+4}{3\sqrt{13}}.\end{aligned}$$
